To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cyanide forms an inhibi-tory complex with the haems of E. coli HPII catalase, and that the rate of binding is controlled by haem accessibility.
cyanide binds to HPII with a low affinity and that HPII N 201D and N201H are cyanide resistant.

cyanide binds to HPII with an affinity similar to that of beef liver catalase, but that the cyanide reaction is much slower, and that cyanide binding requires a distal His, not a distal Asp, but that channel opening to allow cyanide access to the haem may depend on oxidation of the haeme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reaction of cyanide with the haem-containing enzymes of E. coli.
the structure, function and regulation of enzymes that catalyze the disproportionation of hydrogen peroxide to oxygen and water, the so-called catalases.
the mechanism of catalase, a key enzyme in the detoxification of hydrogen peroxide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cyanide binds to the haem d of HPII with an apparent dissociation constant of 7 microM.
HPII N2H1 has two haem groups, one of which is protohaem and one of which is haem d, that cyanide binds to haem d with a Kd of 15 microM, and that cyanide binds with a lower affinity to protohaem.
the cyanide reaction of E. coli enzyme is slow, with low affinity for cyanide and low reactivity with it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cyanide binds weakly to HPII and that the cyanide complex is not an effective inhibitor.
the HPII channel is closed, but that it is openable by peroxide and that it opens to the same degree for the two substrates.
cyanide binding to E. coli HPII requires both distal histidine and haem group oxidation, but not distal asparagines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the catalase reaction with cyanide is slow, but not slow enough to be considered a dead-end reaction.
cyanide binds to HPII with an affinity and kinetics similar to those observed in the bovine enzyme.
the cyanide complex is not a good model of the peroxide complex in catalase HPIII.
